items.title: The Calabi invariant of a Hamiltonian isotopy is twice the total Hamiltonian, under the normalisation
items.author: Alberto Abbondandolo; Christian Lange; Marco Mazzucchelli
items.work: Higher systolic inequalities for 3-dimensional contact manifolds
items.source_version: Journal de l'École polytechnique — Mathématiques 9 (2022), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.195
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `l:Calabi` at source lines 485-491: for a Hamiltonian isotopy generated by a normalised H_t, the integral of the action one-form a_{phi,nu} against omega equals twice the double integral of H_t over the surface. The author's proof (source lines 493-511) is an explicit computation in which three separate ingredients are consumed one after another: the identity a_{phi,nu} = a_{H,nu} and the invariance of omega to move the surface integral inside the time integral (lines 494-498), the rewriting of (X_t interior nu) omega as nu wedge dH_t (line 499), and Stokes theorem applied to H_t dnu - d(H_t nu) to produce the factor two together with a boundary term (lines 502-505). The last step is where the hypothesis enters, since the boundary term vanishes precisely because the Hamiltonian is normalised, and it is evaluated component by component on the boundary components (lines 506-508).
